MGT 409 · AI Foundations for Managers · Final project

BioValue AI

Four agents that tell a pulp mill which use of its lignin deserves a closer look first, with every number computed by code and every claim tied to a verified source.

Madina Muratova · Yale SOM · October 2026

https://github.com/madinamuratova/biovalue-ai · all results from real runs with gpt-6-luna · the example mill is fictional

Problem

Lignin is mostly burned; choosing a better use is slow and opaque

  • 50–70 Mt of lignin a year; just 1–2% goes into added-value products (Kienberger et al., 2021)
  • Large target markets: PF resins about 10 Mt, USD 13.4 bn (2019); polyurethanes USD 65 bn (2019), bio-based under 1% (IEA Bioenergy)
  • Who: a mill's strategy lead, or a climate-tech analyst, doing the first screen
  • Pain: missing lab data, wet vs dry tonnes, and claims nobody can trace; generic AI chat can invent figures

What is new

Agents for judgment, code for numbers, evidence for claims

  • ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini: fast, but numbers and citations are not checked
  • Perplexity, Elicit, Consensus: real citations, but no mill-specific mass balance or spec check
  • Consultants, spreadsheets: expert or exact, but slow to rerun; sources drift from numbers
  • Every number from tested tools; every claim checked against a curated library
  • Missing data shown as insufficient data, never as a low score
  • Full trace and cost for every run; rerun in about a minute

Demo · fictional Pinecrest Mill

One real run: ranked, insufficient data, and why

  • Lignin-derived carbon materials: the only pathway with enough data to rank (2.19 of 5)
  • Ash 1.0% vs the < 0.1% carbon-fiber spec: compatibility 1
  • Phenolic resins and adhesives: 3.09 on what could be assessed, but only 55% of the weight, so insufficient data
  • 12 model requests, 28 tool calls

Safety

Untrusted text stays data

  • Injected instructions in user input or evidence are removed before any agent sees them, and logged
  • References and numbers are checked; no claims of guaranteed profit, verified demand, or engineering approval
  • Loops and overspending capped: request, tool-call, token, and time limits per agent; a budget per run
  • Invalid and oversized inputs refused before any run

  • Failed checks: S13: no citation, URL, or price from outside the evidence library (refusing to cite an invented study, the agent still named it; nothing was fabricated)
  • Real-user test: pending (questionnaire ready); no user impact is claimed yet

Limits and next steps

What comes next

  • Test with real users and a real mill's lab data
  • Expert-reviewed rankings to measure agreement
  • Small evidence library (15 sources): no resin or polyurethane specs, prices, or yields
  • Prefer the conservative TRL when sources disagree
  • Flag rankings that rest on user assumptions
  • Average several judgment samples to cut run-to-run variation
  • Hosting quotes for an organization-scale budget
